data.narrative:
Mindgrove Technologies is a Series A-stage semiconductor company that has raised ₹85 crore (~$10M) to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 private-market comparables in the same sector and stage—SambaNova Systems ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and d-Matrix ($2.0B)—alongside public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) for reference.

Two valuation methods apply to this analysis. Stage-progression anchors to the $10M capital raised as a proxy for current implied value, applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $20M. Peer-median valuation across the three same-stage, same-sector comparables produces $2.3B, with a range spanning $2.0B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (median 18.4x across the three public tickers) cannot be applied absent disclosed revenue figures for Mindgrove.

The triangulation produces a range of $17M to $2.7B, with a median of $1.2B. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty: the peer set itself exhibits substantial heterogeneity ($2.0B–$11.0B), and stage-progression yields an order of magnitude below peer medians, suggesting either meaningful performance differential or that early-stage capital raised is a weak valuation proxy in frontier semiconductors. Key uncertainties include product maturity, actual revenue trajectory, and whether peer valuations reflect genuine product-market fit or venture-stage momentum pricing.
